headline: Decomposers break down the dead—returning nutrients to the living
universal_truth: Endings enable beginnings; breakdown creates raw material for new growth; recycling is essential
fun_facts: A single teaspoon of soil contains more microorganisms than there are people on Earth
Without decomposers, dead matter would pile up—the world would be buried in corpses and waste
Fungi can decompose plastic, oil, and even nuclear waste—they're being studied for environmental cleanup
discussion_questions: What role do you play in 'breaking down' things for reuse?
What endings in your life have created new opportunities?
How do you process and recycle your experiences?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Leaves fall. Animals die. Yet forests aren't buried in corpses. Why? Decomposers: fungi, bacteria, insects that break down the dead and return nutrients to soil. Without them, life would drown in its own waste.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We focus on growth and creation, but breakdown is equally essential. What role do decomposers teach us about systems?

options.text: Decomposers close the loop—they convert endings into beginnings by breaking down the finished into raw materials for new growth
options.response: Yes. Without decomposition, nutrients lock up in dead matter forever. Decomposers liberate those resources for reuse. Breakdown enables growth. Endings create beginnings.

options.text: They just clean up dead things
options.response: Cleanup, yes, but more importantly—they recycle nutrients that life needs...

q1.title: Nutrient Recycling
q1.script: Decomposers don't destroy—they recycle. The nitrogen in a fallen leaf becomes the nitrogen in a growing sprout. Matter cycles endlessly; decomposers are the recycling centers.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Nutrient Recycling"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Invisible Essential
q2.script: Decomposers work invisibly underground or in decay. They're not glamorous, but they're essential. Many crucial functions happen behind the scenes—unappreciated until they stop.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Processing Endings
q3.script: You can be a decomposer too—processing endings into new beginnings. Failed projects into lessons. Old ideas into new insights. The ability to break down and recycle is valuable.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Endings enable beginnings. Breakdown creates raw material for new growth. Learn to decompose—to convert endings into opportunities.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 254. Tomorrow, we'll explore who eats whom—food chains. Until then, consider what you could decompose into something new.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Decomposition Practice - Convert an Ending
growTrack.learning_objective: Transform endings into new raw materials
growTrack.activity: What has recently ended—a project, relationship, phase of life? What 'nutrients' can you extract? Lessons, skills, connections? Consciously decompose endings into raw materials for what's next.
